note.explanation: HTML provides the structure of a web page, CSS controls its appearance, and JavaScript adds behaviour. They work together to create websites.
examples: CSS: p { color: blue; } makes paragraph text blue.
note.simple: Think of a web page as a house: HTML is its structure, CSS is its decoration, and JavaScript makes things happen.
note.checkQuestion: Which language controls the appearance of a web page?
note.title: How HTML, CSS, and JavaScript work together
steps: Use HTML tags to arrange content such as headings, paragraphs, images, and links.
Use CSS rules to style that content.
Use JavaScript to respond to user actions and change page content or appearance.
note.answer: CSS controls the appearance of a web page.

mcqs.stem: Q8.1. Which of the following tag is not a correct HTML tag?  (a) `<div>` (b) `<span>` (c) `<head>` (d) `<footer>`
rationales: The question is defective: `<div>` is a correct HTML tag, just like all the other options, so there is no unique correct answer.
`<span>` is also a valid HTML tag.
`<head>` is also a valid HTML tag.
`<footer>` is also a valid HTML tag.

mcqs.stem: Q8.2. What does CSS stand for?  (a) Cascading Style Sheets (b) Computer Style Sheets  (c) Creative Style Sheets (d) Colorful Style Sheets
rationales: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets.
Computer Style Sheets is not the expansion of CSS.
Creative Style Sheets is not the expansion of CSS.
Colorful Style Sheets is not the expansion of CSS.

mcqs.stem: Q8.3. Which of the following tag is used to create a hyperlink in HTML?  (a) `<link>` (b) `<a>` (c) `<href>` (d) `<nav>`
rationales: `<link>` commonly links external resources, such as a CSS file, rather than creating an ordinary page hyperlink.
The `<a>` tag creates a hyperlink, usually with its destination in the `href` attribute.
`href` is an attribute, not an HTML tag.
`<nav>` marks a navigation section; it does not itself create a hyperlink.

mcqs.stem: Q8.4. Which property is used to change the background color in CSS?  (a) color (b) background-color  (c) bgcolor (d) background
rationales: `color` sets the foreground text color, not specifically the background color.
`background-color` is the CSS property used to set an element's background color.
`bgcolor` is not the standard CSS property for this purpose.
`background` is a shorthand property, but `background-color` is the property specifically for background color.

mcqs.stem: Q8.5. Which HTML attribute is used to define inline styles?  (a) class (b) style (c) font (d) styles
rationales: `class` assigns a class name that can be targeted by CSS; it does not contain the inline style itself.
The `style` attribute contains inline CSS declarations.
`font` is not the HTML attribute used to define inline styles.
`styles` is not the correct attribute; the singular attribute is `style`.

mcqs.stem: Q8.6. Which of the following is the correct syntax for a CSS rule?  (a) `selector {property: value;}` (b) `selector: {property=value;}`  (c) `selector {property=value}` (d) `selector: {property: value;}`
rationales: A CSS rule places declarations inside braces and separates a property from its value with a colon.
This uses an incorrect colon after the selector and an equals sign between the property and value.
This incorrectly uses an equals sign between the property and value.
This incorrectly places a colon after the selector.

mcqs.stem: Q8.7. In JavaScript, which markup is used for comments?  (a) `/* */` (b) `//` (c) `<!--` (d) `/**/`
rationales: `/* ... */` is used for a JavaScript block comment, not the single-line comment asked for here.
`//` begins a single-line JavaScript comment.
`<!--` begins an HTML comment, not the usual JavaScript comment syntax.
`/**/` is not a complete comment form as written; block comments use `/* ... */`.

mcqs.stem: Q8.8. How do you include JavaScript in an HTML document? (a) `` (b) `` (c) `` (d) ``
rationales: The `script` element with its `src` attribute loads an external JavaScript file.
`<java>` is not the HTML element used to load JavaScript.
`<js>` is not the HTML element used to load JavaScript.
`<code>` displays code content; it is not used to load a JavaScript file.

mcqs.stem: Q8.9. Which HTML tag is used to create an unordered list?  (a) `<ol>` (b) `<ul>` (c) `<li>` (d) `<list>`
rationales: `<ol>` creates an ordered list, normally numbered.
`<ul>` creates an unordered list, normally shown with bullets.
`<li>` creates an individual list item inside a list.
`<list>` is not the standard HTML tag for creating a list.

written.text: Q8.1. What is the purpose of the `<head>` tag in HTML?
written.finalAnswer: The `<head>` contains document information and links to resources; its contents are generally not displayed as page content.

rubric.why: The answer should identify the kind of information placed in the head.
rubric.description: Identifies document information or metadata, such as the title.
rubric.how: State that the head contains document information, metadata, or the page title.

rubric.why: This distinguishes the head from the visible body of the page.
rubric.description: Explains that head content is generally not displayed as page content or can link resources.
rubric.how: Mention that it is generally not visible in the page body, or that it links resources such as CSS.

modelAnswer: The `<head>` tag contains information about the HTML document, such as its title and links to resources.
Its contents are generally not displayed as the visible page content.

written.text: Q8.2. Explain the difference between an ordered list and an unordered list in HTML.
written.finalAnswer: An ordered list uses `<ol>` and displays items in a sequence, usually numbered; an unordered list uses `<ul>` and displays items without a numbered sequence, usually with bullets.

rubric.why: The ordered-list tag and its sequence are the first half of the comparison.
rubric.description: Gives `<ol>` and explains that its items have an order, usually numbering.
rubric.how: Name `<ol>` and say its items are numbered or arranged in sequence.

rubric.why: The unordered-list tag and its display complete the comparison.
rubric.description: Gives `<ul>` and explains that its items are usually displayed with bullets.
rubric.how: Name `<ul>` and say its items are not numbered and are usually bulleted.

modelAnswer: An ordered list is written with the `<ol>` tag and displays its items in a sequence, usually with numbers.
An unordered list is written with the `<ul>` tag and displays its items without a numbered sequence, usually with bullets.

written.text: Q8.3. How do you add a comment in CSS?
written.finalAnswer: Write the comment between `/*` and `*/`, for example: `/* This is a comment */`.

rubric.why: The opening marker starts a CSS comment.
rubric.description: Gives the opening CSS comment marker.
rubric.how: Write `/*`.

rubric.why: The closing marker completes the CSS comment syntax.
rubric.description: Gives the closing CSS comment marker.
rubric.how: Write `*/` and show that the comment text is between the two markers.

written.text: Q8.4. What are the different ways to apply CSS to an HTML document?
written.finalAnswer: CSS can be applied inline with the `style` attribute, internally with a `<style>` element, or externally by linking a CSS file.

rubric.why: Inline CSS is one of the main methods of applying CSS.
rubric.description: Names inline CSS and identifies the `style` attribute.
rubric.how: Mention inline styles in the HTML element's `style` attribute.

rubric.why: Internal and external stylesheets are the other main methods.
rubric.description: Names internal CSS and external CSS.
rubric.how: Mention a `<style>` element and/or a linked external stylesheet.

modelAnswer: Inline CSS is written in an HTML element's `style` attribute.
Internal CSS is written inside a `<style>` element, while external CSS is written in a separate file linked to the HTML document.

written.text: Q8.5. How can you include JavaScript in an HTML file?
written.finalAnswer: JavaScript can be written inside a `<script>` element or included from an external file using `<script src="script.js"></script>`.

rubric.why: The script element is the HTML element used to include JavaScript.
rubric.description: Names the `<script>` element.
rubric.how: State that JavaScript is added using `<script>`.

rubric.why: An external script file can be connected through the script element's `src` attribute.
rubric.description: Explains that an external JavaScript file can be linked using `src`.
rubric.how: Give or describe `<script src="script.js"></script>`.

modelAnswer: JavaScript may be written between opening and closing `<script>` tags in the HTML file.
An external file can be included as `<script src="script.js"></script>`.

written.text: Q8.6. Describe the syntax for creating a hyperlink in HTML.
written.finalAnswer: Use `link text`, where `href` gives the destination and the text between the tags is clickable.

rubric.why: The anchor tag and destination attribute form the hyperlink.
rubric.description: Gives the `<a>` tag with an `href` attribute.
rubric.how: Write or describe `<a href="URL">`.

rubric.why: The link text and closing tag complete the hyperlink.
rubric.description: Shows that link text is placed between the opening and closing anchor tags.
rubric.how: Complete the syntax as `link text`.

modelAnswer: Use the anchor tag with the destination in the `href` attribute.

written.text: Q8.7. What is the function of the `<div>` tag in HTML?
written.finalAnswer: The `<div>` tag groups content into a block-level container so that the content can be organised or styled together.

rubric.why: Grouping content is the main purpose of a div.
rubric.description: Explains that `<div>` groups content or acts as a container.
rubric.how: State that it groups elements or content.

rubric.why: The container can be organised and styled as a block.
rubric.description: Mentions its block-level nature or its use in organising or styling content.
rubric.how: Explain that the grouped content can be styled or arranged together.

modelAnswer: The `<div>` tag groups content into a block-level container.
The grouped content can then be organised or styled together.

written.text: Q8.8. How do you link an external CSS file to an HTML document?
written.finalAnswer: Place `<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">` inside the HTML document's `<head>`.

rubric.why: The link element identifies the resource as a stylesheet.
rubric.description: Uses a `<link>` element and a stylesheet relationship.
rubric.how: Include `<link rel="stylesheet"`.

rubric.why: The `href` gives the file location and the link belongs in the head.
rubric.description: Specifies the CSS file with `href` and places the link in the head.
rubric.how: Show `href="style.css"` in the head section.

modelAnswer: Place a link element in the `<head>` section of the HTML document.

written.text: Q8.9. What is the use of the `<table>` tag in HTML?
written.finalAnswer: The `<table>` tag creates a table for displaying data in rows and columns.

rubric.why: The response must identify the element's purpose as creating a table.
rubric.description: States that `<table>` creates or represents a table.
rubric.how: Say that the tag creates a table.

rubric.why: Rows and columns explain how table information is arranged.
rubric.description: Explains that tabular data is arranged in rows and columns.
rubric.how: Mention displaying data in rows and columns.

modelAnswer: The `<table>` tag is used to create a table in HTML.
It displays information as data arranged in rows and columns.

written.text: Q8.10. Explain the box model in CSS.
written.finalAnswer: The CSS box model describes an element as content surrounded by padding, a border, and a margin.

rubric.why: Content and padding are inner parts of the box model.
rubric.description: Names content and padding.
rubric.how: Include content and padding in the model.

rubric.why: Border and margin complete the four main parts.
rubric.description: Names border and margin.
rubric.how: Include border and margin in the model.

modelAnswer: The CSS box model describes each element as a box.
From inside to outside, it consists of content, padding, border, and margin.

written.text: Q8.1. Discuss the fundamental differences between HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in the context of web development.
written.finalAnswer: HTML structures web content, CSS controls its presentation, and JavaScript adds behaviour and interactivity.

rubric.why: A correct account of HTML's role is essential to distinguishing the three technologies.
rubric.description: Explains that HTML provides the structure or content of a page.
rubric.how: Describe HTML as using elements or tags to organise page content.

rubric.why: CSS's presentation role is a central difference.
rubric.description: Explains that CSS controls presentation or appearance.
rubric.how: Mention colours, fonts, layout, or other visual styling.

rubric.why: JavaScript adds behaviour, which differs from structure and styling.
rubric.description: Explains that JavaScript adds behaviour or interactivity.
rubric.how: Give user actions or dynamic changes as examples.

rubric.why: Explaining how the three technologies combine demonstrates the full web-development context.
rubric.description: Connects the three roles in a complete web page.
rubric.how: State that they work together: structure, presentation, and behaviour.

modelAnswer: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) structures the content of a web page using elements such as headings, paragraphs, images, and links.
CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) controls how that content looks, including colours, fonts, spacing, and layout.
JavaScript adds behaviour and interactivity, such as responding when a user clicks a button.
Together, HTML provides the structure, CSS provides the presentation, and JavaScript provides the behaviour of a web page.

written.text: Q8.2. Explain the process of setting up a development environment for web development. By discussing the necessary softwares and tools.
written.finalAnswer: Set up a code editor, a web browser, a project folder, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files; write and save the code, then open the HTML file in the browser to test it.

rubric.why: A code editor is the main tool for writing and editing the web files.
rubric.description: Names a suitable code editor.
rubric.how: Give a code editor as a necessary tool.

rubric.why: A browser displays the page and is needed to test its result.
rubric.description: Names a web browser for viewing and testing the page.
rubric.how: State that a browser is used to open and check the HTML page.

rubric.why: The project needs organised files for its page, styling, and behaviour.
rubric.description: Describes preparing a project folder and relevant web files.
rubric.how: Mention creating or saving HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files.

rubric.why: Testing the saved page is part of setting up a usable development workflow.
rubric.description: Explains how to open and test the work in a browser.
rubric.how: Describe saving the files and checking the HTML page in the browser.

modelAnswer: Install or use a code editor to write and edit HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files.
Use a web browser to display and test the web page.
Create a project folder and save the HTML file and any separate CSS and JavaScript files in it.
Write the code in the editor and save the files.
Open the HTML file in the browser to check the result, then make corrections in the editor as needed.

written.text: Q8.4. How do you style a table using CSS? Create a sample table and apply styles to it.
written.finalAnswer: Create an HTML table and use CSS selectors and declarations to style its borders, cells, headings, and spacing.

rubric.why: The example must have a table structure.
rubric.description: Creates a sample table with rows and cells.
rubric.how: Include table, row, and cell elements.

rubric.why: Table headings or data make the sample meaningful and complete.
rubric.description: Includes suitable table headings and data.

rubric.description: Uses CSS to style borders and cell spacing.

rubric.description: Applies appropriate CSS selectors and an additional visual style.
rubric.how: Style the table or its headings with a selector and a property such as background color or text alignment.

written.text: Q8.5. Describe the different CSS selectors and provide examples of each.
written.finalAnswer: CSS selectors include element, class, ID, and grouping selectors; each selects elements to which the CSS declarations apply.

rubric.why: An element selector is a basic way of selecting HTML elements.
rubric.description: Explains and gives an element selector example.
rubric.how: Give an example such as `p { color: blue; }`.

rubric.why: Class selectors allow the same style to be applied to elements sharing a class.
rubric.description: Explains and gives a class selector example.
rubric.how: Show a class name selected with a dot, such as `.note`.

rubric.why: An ID selector demonstrates selection by an element's ID.
rubric.description: Explains and gives an ID selector example.
rubric.how: Show an ID selected with `#`, such as `#header`.

rubric.why: A grouping selector shows how one rule can select several element types.
rubric.description: Explains and gives a grouping-selector example.
rubric.how: Give a comma-separated example such as `h1, h2`.

modelAnswer: An element selector selects all elements of a specified type: `p { color: blue; }` selects paragraphs.
A class selector selects elements with a specified class and begins with a dot: `.note { color: green; }`.
An ID selector selects an element with a specified ID and begins with `#`: `#header { background-color: gray; }`.
A grouping selector applies one rule to several selectors separated by commas: `h1, h2 { color: navy; }`.

written.text: Q8.6. Explain the process of creating a responsive web page using CSS with the help of examples and explanations.
written.finalAnswer: A responsive page adapts to different screen sizes by using flexible layouts and media queries that change CSS styles at selected widths.

rubric.why: The answer must explain what responsive design achieves.
rubric.description: States that the layout adapts to different screen sizes or devices.
rubric.how: Describe the page adjusting for mobile, tablet, or desktop screens.

rubric.why: Flexible layout choices help content fit different screen widths.
rubric.description: Mentions a flexible layout or sizing approach.
rubric.how: Give a flexible width or layout as an example.

rubric.why: Media queries allow CSS rules to depend on the device or screen dimensions.
rubric.description: Uses a media query in the explanation or example.
rubric.how: Write an `@media` rule with a screen-width condition.

rubric.why: A specific responsive change demonstrates how the technique works.
rubric.description: Gives an appropriate change for a smaller screen.
rubric.how: For example, change a multi-column layout to one column at a smaller width.

modelAnswer: A responsive web page adjusts its layout to suit different screen sizes, such as phones, tablets, and computers.
Use flexible dimensions and layouts so that the content can fit different available widths.
A media query applies CSS only when its condition is met.
In this example, the container uses 80% width normally and changes to 100% width when the screen is 600 pixels wide or less.

written.text: Q8.7. Write a JavaScript function that changes the background color of a web page when a button is clicked. Provide the complete code and explain how it works.
written.finalAnswer: A page with a button whose click event runs a JavaScript function that changes the document background color.

rubric.why: The user needs a button to initiate the change.
rubric.description: Includes a button in the page.
rubric.how: Write a button element with suitable text.

rubric.why: A function and click handling connect the user's action to the change.
rubric.description: Defines or invokes a function in response to a button click.
rubric.how: Use an onclick handler or a click event listener.

rubric.why: The code must change the page's background colour.
rubric.description: Changes the body background colour in JavaScript.
rubric.how: Set `document.body.style.backgroundColor` to a colour.

rubric.why: An explanation of the event and result shows understanding of the code.
rubric.description: Explains that clicking the button runs the function and changes the background.
rubric.how: Describe the click event and the resulting colour change.

modelAnswer: When the button is clicked, `changeColor()` runs.
The function sets the background color of the page body to light blue.

written.text: Q8.8. How do you add animations and transitions using CSS? Provide examples and explain the properties involved.
written.finalAnswer: CSS transitions smoothly change a property between states, while CSS animations use keyframes to define a sequence of style changes over time.

rubric.why: The response should explain the purpose of a transition.
rubric.description: Explains that a transition smoothly changes a property between states.
rubric.how: Describe a smooth change and name a property such as `transition`.

rubric.why: A working transition example needs a property and a time or duration.
rubric.description: Provides an example of a transition declaration.
rubric.how: Give a declaration such as `transition: background-color 0.5s;`.

rubric.why: Keyframes define the stages of a CSS animation.
rubric.description: Explains or demonstrates animation using keyframes.
rubric.how: Show an `@keyframes` rule with at least one animation stage.

rubric.why: The animation property applies and controls the defined keyframes.
rubric.description: Applies an animation and names a relevant animation property.
rubric.how: Give an animation declaration with a name and duration.

modelAnswer: A transition smoothly changes a CSS property when its value changes.
The `transition` property gives the background-color change a duration of 0.5 seconds.
An animation uses keyframes to describe stages of a change over time.
The `@keyframes` rule defines the movement from the starting position to the ending position.
The `animation` property applies the animation and sets its name and duration.

examTips: Short questions often ask for a tag, attribute, property, or syntax; give the correct name and a brief example to secure both marks.
For compare-and-explain questions, state both sides clearly, using the correct HTML tags such as `<ol>` and `<ul>`.
Long questions that ask for code should include complete opening and closing tags, correctly placed attributes, and the requested elements or styles.
For CSS questions, use the rule format `selector {property: value;}` and show where each rule applies.
For longer explanations, define the idea, give a correct code example, and explain how the example works; these are separate opportunities to earn marks.

explain.title: HTML gives a page its structure
explain.body: HTML tags organise content into elements such as headings, paragraphs, images, lists, links, and tables.

explain.title: CSS controls the appearance
explain.body: CSS rules use a selector and declarations in braces, for example `p { color: blue; }`. CSS can be inline, internal, or external.

explain.title: JavaScript adds behaviour
explain.body: JavaScript can respond to events such as button clicks. A `<script>` element can contain code or load an external file using `src`.

explain.title: HTML links and lists use particular tags
explain.body:
Use `text` for a hyperlink. Use `
    ` for an ordered list and `
      ` for an unordered list; put list items in `
    • ` tags.

explain.title: CSS changes layout and effects
explain.body: The box model has content, padding, border, and margin. Responsive CSS can adapt a layout with flexible sizing and media queries; transitions and animations add movement.

mistakes: Do not confuse an HTML tag with an attribute: `<a>` is a tag, while `href` is an attribute.
Do not write CSS property and value with an equals sign; use a colon inside the braces.
Do not confuse `color` with `background-color`; they affect different parts of an element.
Remember that `<ol>` is ordered and `<ul>` is unordered.
When linking an external CSS file, use a `<link>` element with `rel="stylesheet"` and `href` in the document head.
In code questions, check that tags are properly opened and closed and that every requested element is present.
The first Section A question is defective: all four listed options are valid HTML tags, so it has no unique correct option.
